title: Joining Goodman: flying to Columbus
summary: Flight to Columbus in 1939 and the teen-idol atmosphere around Goodman's band.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: In which case, I suppose we have to try to get back to Benny Goodman,
I believe you said on Monday that that John Hammond had called you to come and work for Benny, and this was in 1939; correct?
What transpired from then? Did you have any kind of negotiating between you and John or you and Benny, about music or money, or anything like that?
Very little, no. That was not a concern of mine in those days. My main concern was leaving Red. I truly didn't want to do that and something told me to do it.
I remember flying out to Columbus in one of those crates they used to have, very early in the airline scene, and they flew right over the tree tops and they gave you box lunches.
So I arrived in Columbus and

the town is jumping, they've got banners, it's like an American Legion convention. The band welcomed Benny; big deal. I couldn't get over it; I had never seen anything like that. It was very much like the rock scene today, not too different. The scale was different, but other than that it was pretty much the same.
It was shocking to walk in, because I never expected anything like that.
Red Norvo wasn't a teen idol.
